transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Evelyn Chen (Redwood SE), Laila Ahmad (Orion - Head of ML), Martin Reyes (Orion - Platform), Sasha Brody (Orion - CISO)

Summary: quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Discussed workload sizing, benchmarks (latency/throughput/cost), go/no-go thresholds, reporting format, and timelines. Action items captured at end.

Topics: 1) Success criteria / go-no-go thresholds 2) Workload sizing and sample data 3) Benchmark plan and reporting 4) Security/compliance acceptance items 5) Timeline and next steps

[00:00] Samir: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, with Evelyn from our SE team. We're here to finalize the POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we have a clean go/no-go at the end of the run.
[00:18] Laila: Thanks, Samir. Appreciate it. We had the internal stakeholders review the draft SOW, just want to make sure the acceptance tests map to our platform KPIs.
[00:28] Evelyn: Yeah totally. Quick note, the deck I posted earlier has the test matrix - link in chat: https://redwood.ai/poc/orion-deck (note: placeholder). We'll walk through the thresholds we proposed.
[00:40] Martin: One quick ask, when you say latency thresholds are you talking end-to-end (app -> model -> response) or just model inference time? For us we care E2E.
[00:51] Samir: Good question. We can measure both. For go/no-go we recommend E2E p95 < 800ms for the primary customer-facing route, and model-side p95 < 500ms as a technical pass. Those numbers are adjustable but are tied to cost/throughput tradeoffs.
[01:10] Sasha: From a security standpoint we also need audit logs and key management validation during the POC. Can that be part of acceptance?
[01:20] Evelyn: Yes, we'll include a security checklist as part of the acceptance tests - SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration proof, and log delivery to your SIEM. We'll document expected artifacts and validation steps.
[01:34] Laila: Okay cool. Let's walk through the success criteria one by one.

--- Success criteria discussion ---
[01:44] Samir: Criterion A - Latency: E2E p95 < 800ms for the canonical prompt set under the target QPS (we'll define QPS in sizing). Technical model inference p95 < 500ms. If p95 is between 800 and 1200ms this becomes a warning but not an auto-fail; above 1200ms is a fail.
[02:10] Laila: Sounds reasonable, can we get p50 targets too? Our UX team likes median numbers.
[02:16] Evelyn: Yes p50 target of < 150ms model-side, E2E p50 < 300ms.
[02:23] Martin: For throughput, what's the target? We have bursty traffic but average about 60 QPS on the routes we'll test.
[02:30] Samir: For the POC we'll size for sustained 60 QPS and a 2x burst to 120 QPS for 5 minutes to validate autoscaling. The throughput acceptance is that 95% of requests during steady-state sustainment should succeed without model fallback and maintain the latency thresholds.
[02:47] Laila: Ok and cost? We need to compare to our current vendor spend.
[02:52] Samir: We'll provide a cost model in the SOW, but as an acceptance metric we'll include a target unit cost: cost per 1M tokens < $X (placeholder) compared to your baseline. The exact dollar figure we'll agree in the SOW after you share baseline numbers.
[03:10] Martin: There's also accuracy/regression - we run some NER and Q&A tasks. How do you want us to measure quality?
[03:18] Evelyn: We suggest a small evaluation suite: 500 labeled examples across tasks (NER, intent, Q&A). Acceptance: no more than 3% drop in F1/accuracy compared to baseline. If quality regresses more than that, it's a fail unless we can adjust prompts/model variant.
[03:33] Laila: Good. And how will you report tokenization differences? We've seen subtle tokenization causing cost spikes.
[03:40] Samir: We'll include token-level accounting in the benchmark report, with per-route token means and percentiles. We'll also surface any tokenization mismatches in a short appendix.

--- Benchmark test plan ---
[03:52] Samir: The benchmark will be run in two phases: 1) Smoke and functional verification with small sample set 2) Full load benchmark with traffic replay of your traces and the canonical prompt set.
[04:05] Evelyn: We'll use your traffic traces to drive the load generator. Link to test harness and how to format logs: https://redwood.ai/poc/harness (placeholder). We prefer you upload sanitized traces to the secure S3 bucket we'll send.
[04:20] Martin: We can sanitize and provide traces, but timeline wise we need to know when to deliver them.
[04:27] Samir: Deadline for traces: 2025-10-06 so we can run the first full benchmark the week of 10/7.
[04:34] Laila: Works. Will the benchmarks include KV cache / prefix caching behavior? We rely on conversation history caching a lot.
[04:41] Evelyn: Yes we'll exercise prefix/KV cache scenarios. Note: sometimes transcripts show K-V cash or K V cache in the automation logs — just warning that auto-transcribe may miss hyphens.
[04:54] (laughter)

[05:00] Samir: We'll also test quantized model variants for cost comparisons if you want. That will be an additional axis: accuracy vs unit cost.
[05:10] Laila: Please do. That decision point is key for us.

--- Acceptance reporting format ---
[05:20] Evelyn: For the final report we'll produce a short executive summary (1 page) and a technical appendix. Executive: go/no-go statement with pass/fail per criterion, cost delta vs baseline, and recommended model/config. Technical appendix: raw latency/throughput percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token accounting, error rates, and the evaluation results for the labeled dataset. We'll deliver the report as PDF plus a CSV/JSON of raw metrics.
[05:46] Martin: CSV/JSON is important - platform team will ingest into our dashboards.
[05:51] Samir: Agreed. We'll provide both. We'll also give a reproducible runbook with the exact commands we used.

[06:06] Sasha: Security items - we need proof of KMS integration, key rotation policy, audit log export to our SIEM, and proof that data does not persist beyond configured TTL.
[06:18] Evelyn: We'll include those in the security checklist. For KMS we'll do a demo connection using your staging KMS and show envelope encryption. We'll also provide SOC2 docs and our standard security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security (placeholder).
[06:34] Sasha: For audit logs, do you support streaming to syslog/Splunk?
[06:38] Samir: Yes we can stream to your SIEM or drop S3 exports. We'll work out retention policies in the SOW.

--- Timelines and go/no-go cadence ---
[06:48] Samir: Proposed timeline:
 - 10/03: SOW and pricing sign-off
 - 10/06: Customer provides workload traces and labeled test set
 - 10/07-10/09: Smoke tests and lab setup
 - 10/10-10/14: Full benchmark runs and iteration
 - 10/15: Final report and go/no-go decision meeting
[07:10] Laila: The 10/15 date is fine but can we shift one week if we hit blockers?
[07:14] Samir: Yes we can be flexible, it's a target.

--- Example acceptance test thresholds (recap) ---
[07:22] Evelyn: Recap of go/no-go thresholds we'll include in the SOW: 
 - Quality: no more than 3% relative drop in F1/accuracy on labeled test set
 - Latency: E2E p95 < 800ms (warning 800-1200ms, fail >1200ms); model-side p95 < 500ms
 - Throughput: sustain 60 QPS steady-state with 2x burst to 120 QPS for 5 minutes without fallback
 - Availability: 99.5% successful responses during benchmark window
 - Cost: unit cost per 1M tokens within agreed delta to baseline (exact number in SOW)
 - Security/compliance: KMS integration + audit logs validated, SOC2 artifacts provided
[07:57] Martin: For availability, do you count HTTP 429 as fail?
[08:00] Samir: Yes 4xx/5xx and explicit fallbacks count as failures. Rate-limit induced 429s during steady-state are considered fails for acceptance; during controlled burst they are tolerated up to a small percentage (we'll define in the SOW, suggested 1%).

[08:18] Laila: Reporting format - will you include time series plots and confidence intervals?
[08:23] Evelyn: Yes, timeseries with rolling percentiles, boxplots for token usage, and error histograms. We'll attach raw JSON for ingestion.

--- Questions & clarifications ---
[08:33] Martin: A couple of practical bits: Do you need network egress estimates? We send a lot of embeddings out.
[08:38] Samir: We'll model egress in the cost appendix. If you share sample embedding sizes and QPS we can estimate.
[08:45] (small cross-talk)
[08:49] Laila: One more point - rollback criteria post-POC if we move to Dedicated; who owns rollback plan?
[08:56] Evelyn: We'll propose an incremental rollout and a fallback to hosted model variant. The rollback runbook is part of the deliverables if you proceed to Dedicated.

--- Noise / transcript artifacts ---
[09:05] (note: auto-transcription sometimes lists Speaker 2 where we had the AE; ignore minor speaker attribution differences)

--- Final recap and explicit next steps ---
[09:15] Samir: Recap: we'll update the SOW with thresholds we agreed (latency, quality, throughput, security items). Samir sends SOW + pricing by 10/03. Evelyn will stand up the test harness and run smoke by 10/07. Laila provides traces and labeled dataset by 10/06. Sasha confirms compliance artifacts by 10/07. Final report aimed for 10/15 and then we'll do go/no-go.
[09:44] Laila: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:46] Sasha: Thanks, appreciate the security detail.
[09:49] Martin: We'll get the traces sanitized and uploaded.
[09:52] Samir: Great, action items in the chat. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.

(End of recorded portion - remainder was side conversation about calendar slots and a quick demo scheduling which was not recorded in full.)
